titulo: Έχετε and μπορώ να — the desk minute that improves the room
subtitulo: Check-in is the one minute when the list is still open and asking costs you nothing
cena: Reception, late morning. The key is in someone's hand, the room is not ready, and everything you would like about the next three nights is still negotiable.
frasePiso: Έχετε for what they have, μπορώ να for what you want to do. Two openings run the whole desk.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: In Greece a consumer-to-business invoice of €500 or more cannot be settled in cash: it has to be paid by card, transfer or another electronic means. The ceiling was lowered to €500 from the earlier €1,500. Below that figure cash is still cash — the rule bites at the total, which is exactly where a hotel bill tends to land.
fatosDatados.fonte: Teto de espécie: €500 para consumidor→empresa — art. 69 §2 do ν.4446/2016, que reduziu o limite anterior de €1.500. Fatura de valor igual ou superior a €500 tem de ser paga por cartão, transferência ou meio eletrônico.

steps.pt: Check-in lasts about a minute, and it is the cheapest minute of the whole stay. The list is still open.
Two openings run this desk. Έχετε for what they have, μπορώ να for what you would like to do.

steps.es: Καλώς ήρθατε! Το διαβατήριό σας, παρακαλώ.
steps.pt: Welcome! Your passport, please.
steps.tts: Καλώς ήρθατε! Το διαβατήριό σας, παρακαλώ.

steps.promptPt: You have just walked in with your bag and the desk is looking up at you. Open the check-in. Speak now.
steps.pt: Good morning, I have a booking.
Ask for the improvement first, before anything else. Quieter, higher, later — in that order.

steps.promptPt: The street outside has two bars on it and you are here for three nights. Ask at the desk. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have a quieter room?

steps.es: Έχω ένα στον τρίτο, προς την αυλή.
steps.pt: I have one on the third floor, facing the courtyard.
steps.tts: Έχω ένα στον τρίτο, προς την αυλή.
steps.acao: The yes arrived as a floor and a direction. Take the courtyard side and say thank you.

steps.pt: The answer often lands as a floor number rather than as a yes. Take the number, it is the yes.

steps.promptPt: The room you were given is on the ground floor, right beside the front door. Ask. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have anything on a higher floor?
Bags come before rooms. A room that is ready at two does not have to cost you the morning.

steps.promptPt: It is eleven, the room is ready at two, and you would rather not spend three hours holding a suitcase. Speak now.
steps.es: Μπορώ να αφήσω τη βαλίτσα εδώ;
steps.pinyin: bo-RO na a-FEE-so ti va-LEE-tsa e-THO
steps.pt: Can I leave my suitcase here?
steps.tts: Μπορώ να αφήσω τη βαλίτσα εδώ;

steps.es: Βεβαίως, αφήστε την πίσω από τον πάγκο.
steps.pt: Of course, leave it behind the counter.
steps.tts: Βεβαίως, αφήστε την πίσω από τον πάγκο.

steps.promptPt: Your flight tomorrow is in the evening and check-out is at eleven. Ask now, while they are still typing. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can I leave later tomorrow?

steps.promptPt: Your plug has three flat pins and every socket in the room has two round holes. Ask at the desk. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have an adapter?

steps.promptPt: Fourth floor, one heavy bag, and the staircase is the only thing you can see. Speak now.
steps.pt: I'm looking for the lift.

steps.promptPt: You want to know whether tomorrow starts with coffee downstairs or with a walk. Ask. Speak now.
steps.pt: What time is breakfast?

steps.es: Το πρωινό είναι από τις εφτά ως τις δέκα.
steps.pt: Breakfast is from seven until ten.
steps.tts: Το πρωινό είναι από τις εφτά ως τις δέκα.
steps.acao: Two numbers went past. Write down the second one — it is the deadline, not the invitation.

steps.pt: Now the half that goes wrong. Name the thing, then say it is not working. Two words, no story.

steps.promptPt: Thirty-four degrees outside, the unit on the wall hums and blows nothing. Back at the desk. Speak now.
steps.pt: The air conditioning isn't working.

steps.promptPt: You have had the shower tap on for four minutes and it is still cold. Phone the desk. Speak now.
steps.pt: There's no hot water.
I'll send someone right away.

steps.promptPt: You have named the thing and nothing has moved yet. Get someone up there with their own eyes on it. Speak now.
steps.pt: Could you have a look at it, please?
One number to keep: a bill of five hundred euros or more has to go on a card, never in cash.
None of this needs a complaint voice. A room is a machine, and machines get reported flatly.

steps.es: Έχετε ένα πιο ήσυχο δωμάτιο; Μπορώ να αφήσω τη βαλίτσα εδώ; Δεν έχει ζεστό νερό.
steps.pinyin: EH-kheh-teh EH-na pyo EE-si-kho tho-MA-ti-o. bo-RO na a-FEE-so ti va-LEE-tsa e-THO. then EH-khi ze-STO ne-RO
steps.pt: Shadow the ask, the favour and the report — the three shapes the desk answers.
steps.tts: Έχετε ένα πιο ήσυχο δωμάτιο; Μπορώ να αφήσω τη βαλίτσα εδώ; Δεν έχει ζεστό νερό.

steps.pt: B16 done. Έχετε, μπορώ να, and two flat sentences for anything upstairs that has stopped.

secoes.titulo: Ask before the key changes hands
secoes.corpo: Quieter, higher, later. Those three requests cost one keystroke while the booking is still on the screen, and they turn into a favour needing a reason once you have been given a key and walked away. The order matters too: ask for the room you want, then ask for the bag to be kept, then ask about tomorrow morning.

exemplos.pt: Do you have a quieter room?

secoes.corpo: Έχετε asks what this person has: a quieter room, an adapter, a socket, a map. Μπορώ να asks whether an action of yours is allowed: leaving the bag, leaving later, going up now. Almost everything at a reception desk is one or the other, and neither opening changes shape whatever you put after it.

A yes here often arrives as a detail rather than as the word yes — στον τρίτο, προς την αυλή, στις δύο. Third floor, courtyard side, at two. Listen past the first syllable for the floor, the side or the hour, because that is the actual answer and it is also the thing you need to remember.

secoes.titulo: Saying a thing is broken without a scene
secoes.corpo: Name the object, add δεν δουλεύει — it does not work. Το κλιματιστικό δεν δουλεύει. Η τηλεόραση δεν δουλεύει. For water and light, δεν έχει does the job: δεν έχει ζεστό νερό, there is no hot water. Then μπορείτε να το δείτε; brings someone up to look. Flat delivery is not rudeness; it is the register that gets a technician sent.

A consumer bill of €500 or more cannot legally be settled in cash in Greece — card, transfer or another electronic means, and the limit came down from €1,500. Three or four nights plus extras can cross that line without feeling like it. Carry the card you intend to pay with, and expect the total, not each night, to be what counts.

permissao: You are allowed to ask for a better room without a reason, at the moment you arrive, in eight words. Nobody at that desk thinks a request is a complaint, and nobody is keeping score of how many you make — and if the answer is no, you have lost exactly the second it took to ask.
espelho: Anyone who has ever checked into a hotel at home has felt the same small hesitation about asking for a different room, and has usually swallowed it and slept badly beside a lift shaft. The only new part is that here the hesitation costs you eight Greek words instead of eight English ones.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You open at the desk with your request straight away, in English, and the reply comes back short and businesslike — and the whole exchange feels cooler than you expected.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: They would rather I were not here, or my English is unwelcome.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Research comparing politeness in England and Greece describes the two systems as oriented in opposite directions: Greek interaction leans on involvement and closeness, English on distance and non-imposition. The predictable result is symmetrical misreading — one side reads the other as abrupt, the other reads back as cool. Both readings are artefacts of the difference.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Lead with καλησπέρα or καλημέρα on its own, let it be answered, and only then say what you need. Keep your own request short rather than padding it with conditionals — the padding is what reads as distance here.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: The exchange starts on the footing the other person expects, and the request that follows is heard as a request rather than as an intrusion.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: This describes a documented difference between two politeness systems, not a personality. It does not predict any individual desk, and a short answer at the end of a long shift with a queue behind you is sometimes just a short answer.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You offer to settle the bill in cash at the end of a longer stay and the desk points at the card machine instead.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: They prefer card for their own reasons, or they are pushing a fee onto me.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: A consumer-to-business invoice of €500 or more cannot be paid in cash in Greece: the law requires card, transfer or another electronic means, and the ceiling was lowered to €500 from €1,500. The desk is not choosing; the total crossed a line.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Decide before you arrive which card is paying for the room, and keep cash for the small things — coffee, taxis, the kiosk. If you want to split, ask at check-in rather than at check-out.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You stop planning a big cash payment that cannot legally happen, and the last morning has one fewer thing to sort out.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: It is a rule about the invoice total, not a ban on cash. Below the line cash works normally, and it says nothing about tips, kiosks or a coffee downstairs.
